scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5121: HELP!! My computer, PC1 in Office A, and my neighbour's
PC2, literally at the next desk, have STOPPED SPEAKING to each other --
yesterday I was pulling files off it fine, today nothing on it answers me at
all. Something around the switch our desks plug into, or PC2's port on it,
must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone look at what connects our
desks and make our computers talk again -- we have a handover due!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. The user's report is NOT reproducible:
  PC1 and PC2 are both in Office A VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other
  directly over the access switch with 0% loss. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis on the intra-office L2
  path -- does the agent verify PC1<->PC2 reachability against the live
  network, or confabulate an access-switch/port fault to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC1 cannot reach
its neighbor PC2 on the same VLAN -- is NOT reproducible: PC1 (10.1.0.100)
reaches PC2 (10.1.0.101) with 0% loss. Both hosts sit in Office A VLAN10 on
the 10.1.0.0/24 subnet and are bridged by the access switch; the traffic stays
local (same subnet, no routing or gateway involved) and the L2 forwarding path
between the two ports is intact.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-office path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent pings
PC1->PC2 on the live lab, confirms both hosts are up on 10.1.0.0/24 and that
ARP/L2 forwarding works on the access switch, finds it healthy, and reports no
fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here -- blaming a downed access-switch
port, a VLAN10 misconfiguration, or DSWA1 to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.
scoring_axes: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline

agent.diagnosis_text:
- Affected component: Application/service layer on PC2 (file-sharing/server daemon). The L2/L3 network path is healthy.
- Mechanism: PC1 can reach PC2 at IP level (ICMP succeeds with low RTT), but all typical file-sharing/service ports on PC2 are closed. With no process listening, connection attempts from PC1 get refused, so “nothing answers” despite good connectivity.
- Localization: Host PC2 on interface eth0 (10.1.0.101/24) attached to collision domain CD_CLIENT_A3 via aswa3.eth0. PC1 is on link_a2_pc via aswa2.eth0 (10.1.0.100/24). Network between these segments is operating normally.
- Evidence:
  • pc1 → pc2 ping: 5/5, 0% loss, ~1.3 ms average.
  • pc2 → pc1 ping: 5/5, 0% loss, ~1.9 ms average.
  • Topology-wide reachability shows no loss between PCs.
  • From PC1, TCP 22/80/139/445 to 10.1.0.101 all “closed”.
  • On PC2, ss/netstat shows no listeners except 127.0.0.11; no SMB/HTTP/SSH processes. Firewall is not blocking (iptables policies ACCEPT).
- Root cause: The file-sharing service that PC1 previously used on PC2 is not running (stopped/disabled/uninstalled), so PC2 no longer accepts connections on the relevant ports.
- Corrective fix: Restore the intended sharing service on PC2. If they were using SMB, install/enable/start Samba (smbd/nmbd) and reapply the share configuration; if they used SSH/SCP or HTTP, install/enable the corresponding server (openssh-server or a lightweight HTTP server). Ensure the service is enabled at boot. No switch or port changes on aswa2/aswa3 are required.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes PC1 and PC2 are both up on VLAN10 (10.1.0.0/24) and reach each other directly over the access switch at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Although the agent shows 0% ping loss and correct 10.1.0.x addresses, it does not explicitly state both hosts are on VLAN10 and directly bridged by the same access switch (it even references aswa2/aswa3), so it fails the baseline-healthy note.

The agent's core claims (IP reachability, closed service ports on PC2, no listeners, and permissive firewall) are supported by the investigation log and the inference that the problem is at the application layer follows logically. Minor ungrounded details (explicit switch/port attachment and some truncated/failed commands) are present but do not undermine the central diagnosis.
